analysis.title: Growing Pains: Goldman's 2027 Playbook Says Buy Bonds, Short The Euro, And Hedge The AI Hangover
key_insights: Goldman's Global Markets Outlook 2027 "Growing Pains" (Wilson, Trivedi) forecasts stable growth, falling inflation, peaking policy rates and positive returns for both stocks and bonds, but says the market cycle is showing its age: real rates are higher, credit spreads wider and volatility rising under the surface.
AI accounted for about 21% of true US GDP growth this year including spillovers, 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth and at the peak 92% of the gain in S&P 500 market cap (41% year-to-date).

Goldman puts the peak in the AI investment impulse (additional AI investment as a share of GDP) in early 2027. It calls this a manageable event for the economy but a bigger test for markets, because AI has contributed far more to earnings and market value than to GDP.
Global AI capex rises from roughly $1 trillion this year to about $1.8 trillion in 2027, but the US AI capex contribution to growth peaks near 2pp in Q1 2027 and falls toward zero by late 2028.
S&P 500 earnings are about 8% of GDP versus a 1995-present trend near 6%. Goldman expects S&P earnings growth to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027.

Goldman's pessimistic scenario is a bigger aggregate shock via three paths: the market looks ahead to the 2028 peak in investment share, the baton passes too slowly to other sectors, or financial and credit feedback loops accelerate faster than baseline. It says the most likely channel for AI worries to hurt the economy is financial conditions themselves.

Goldman says the credit underperformance it expected in 2026 only became clear in recent months and financing needs are likely to build further in 2027. It sees record US credit issuance above $2.5 trillion in both 2026 and 2027 alongside heavy equity supply.

AI-related USD IG spreads are about 140bp, near where non-AI spreads peaked in April 2025, versus about 100bp for everything else. Goldman calls for further modest widening in index-level credit spreads with skew to the wider side, and says hyperscaler free cash flow has deteriorated sharply.

Valuation exhibit: real yields on A/BBB credit are in the 77th percentile since 1999 and 10-year TIPS in the 86th, while the S&P cyclically adjusted earnings yield is in the 6th percentile and the equity risk premium in the 8th.

Duration is Goldman's most constructive asset call: decent running yield, underweight positioning, cheap valuations and signs higher real rates are hard to sustain. It sees the UST 10Y at 4.6% by end-2027 versus roughly 5.1% now.

Stock-bond correlation had turned sharply negative but the 1-week correlation moved from about -0.55 back toward zero. Tuesday's hot core CPI and Thursday's weak 30Y auction hit stocks and bonds together, and Goldman's economists added a hike after the CPI print.

Energy: Goldman's base case is a gradual decline in oil with Brent toward the high-$70s by late 2027, roughly in line with forwards. An upside escalation case peaks above $130 next spring. Its estimated risk premium swung from about +$25/bbl in late October to roughly zero after the midterms, and Brent is back near $96.
Goldman likes TTF call spreads as a hedge into Europe's precarious winter. Dutch gas is up almost 11% this week.

FX: Goldman forecasts a roughly 3% fall in the broad trade-weighted dollar in 2027, with US tech the swing factor. If US tech exceptionalism erodes it expects the dollar to sell off rather than gain a safe-haven bid, with the yen as the real haven. It stays bearish on the euro until France's spring election.
2027 baseline returns: global equities low double digits in local currency, DM government bonds about 6%, credit about the same, cash nearly 4%, commodities slightly negative.

Hedging menu: receive rates in the US and Japan or position for jointly lower rates and equities, USD/JPY downside, European gas futures, TTF call spreads and EUR funding, and out-of-the-money equity puts or replacing stock holdings with longer-dated calls. Goldman says equity index volatility is unlikely to fall much and could rise if macro stresses broaden.

The article's author (not Goldman) leans toward the path where financial conditions tighten first and argues puts are warranted given the 8th percentile equity risk premium. Goldman's equity analysts say Jensen Huang's exit will have a measured direct impact on Nvidia given its 12-24 month backlog.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell as much as 14% at Thursday's open after Jensen Huang's exit. Goldman equity analysts expect a measured direct impact given a 12-24 month backlog. Nvidia reports Tuesday under an interim CEO.

sector_views.rationale: The AI investment impulse peaks in early 2027 and equities are more exposed to the deceleration than GDP. AI infrastructure names have been sliding since June and the market is pricing peak capex.
Goldman expects further widening in index-level spreads with a skew to wider. AI-related issuers trade at about 140bp versus about 100bp for others.
Running yield, underweight positioning, cheap valuations and a 10Y forecast of 4.6% by end-2027 from roughly 5.1% now.

earnings_insights: Goldman forecast: S&P 500 earnings growth slows from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027, described as still robust. This is a forecast.
S&P 500 earnings are roughly 8% of GDP versus a 1995-present trend near 6%. Goldman's key question is how much of that proves persistent as the investment cycle fades.
AI accounted for 62% of S&P 500 earnings growth this year, via hyperscalers and AI infrastructure.
Nvidia is scheduled to report Tuesday, per the article. No consensus figures are given.

risk_factors: A sharper AI reversal, with the market looking ahead to the 2028 peak in investment share.
The baton passing too slowly from AI infrastructure to other sectors.
Financial and credit conditions feedback loops accelerating faster than baseline.
Energy shock extending, or an escalation-driven oil spike above $130.
Stickier inflation and a more resilient labour market, which would push rates higher.
Credit spread widening, with hyperscaler free cash flow deteriorating sharply.
France's budget crisis and a possible bond crisis.
Stock-bond correlation reverting toward zero, so bonds hedge AI scares but not inflation scares.
charts_described: AI share of US GDP growth (about 21%), S&P 500 earnings growth (62%) and market cap gain (92%), per the article text.
Goldman Exhibit 3: global AI capex from roughly $1 trillion to about $1.8 trillion in 2027, with the US contribution to growth peaking near 2pp in Q1 2027.
Valuation exhibit: A/BBB real yields in the 77th percentile, 10-year TIPS in the 86th, CAPE earnings yield in the 6th and equity risk premium in the 8th.
vol_and_positioning: Sharpest volatility has been under the surface of the major equity indices. Index volatility has risen a little, is unlikely to fall much, and has scope to rise if macro stresses broaden.
Goldman says deeper protection in equities themselves seems more valuable than usual as the cycle matures.
Goldman says bonds are underweight in positioning.
AI-related USD IG spreads are about 140bp versus about 100bp for everything else.
Hedging ideas: out-of-the-money equity puts, longer-dated calls replacing stock holdings, TTF call spreads, USD/JPY downside.
geopolitical: Oil war and energy shock this year, with the conflict involving Iran. Goldman's base case is gradual oil declines even without full resolution, and it calls an escalation-driven spike one of the largest near-term risks.
Trump says the US does not need a deal with Iran (per Bloomberg).
France's spring election and an unaddressed budget mess weigh on the euro.
Europe's precarious winter and Dutch gas up almost 11% this week.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's base case is a rotation. Gains move down the waterfall to hyperscalers if monetization shows up, AI adopters and non-AI companies, helped by lower oil and yields, with S&P earnings growth still 11% in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A bigger aggregate shock if the market looks ahead to the 2028 investment-share peak, the baton passes too slowly, or financial and credit feedback loops accelerate. AI-related IG spreads are already about 140bp and the equity risk premium is in the 8th percentile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further credit spread widening or tightening financial conditions, with oil, yields and credit moving the wrong way, would break the baton-pass case.

tension_points.bull_case: Duration is Goldman's most constructive call, with the 10Y falling to 4.6% by end-2027 and negative stock-bond correlation as AI pressure replaces energy pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: The 1-week stock-bond correlation snapped back toward zero. Hot core CPI and a poor 30Y auction hit stocks and bonds together, and the market could stay hawkish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The energy shock extending further, or inflation staying stickier with a resilient labour market, as it did this year.
